title: Default Environment Design
hook: Discipline isn't your problem. Your setup makes the wrong thing the easy thing.
statement: Defaults drive behavior. Set them up right and you barely need willpower.
explainer: Most of what you do is just the path of least resistance. If the easy option is the wrong one, you'll fight yourself all day and usually lose.
sop: Walk through your space and apps. Note the easiest path for each habit.
Score Default Appeal and Friction from 1 to 10 for the behavior you want.
Remove friction from what you want: auto-pay, prepped food, pinned apps.
Add friction to what you don't: delete the app, hide the snacks.
Re-check monthly. Old shortcuts sneak back in.
equation_example: Default Appeal 8, Friction 2. 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Higher means your environment does the work for you. Lower means you're leaning on discipline to fight a bad default.
question: Write down one default in your space or on your phone that's working against you.
closing_statement: Design the default so willpower isn't needed.
caption:
Principle Nº 195: Default Environment Design

Discipline isn't your problem. Your setup makes the wrong thing the easy thing.

Defaults drive behavior. Set them up right and you barely need willpower.

Your turn: Write down one default in your space or on your phone that's working against you.
